COMPOUND_EXISTENCE_GATE_RE's 'no captured output' rule only recognises `test -f/-e X && ...` and `[ -f/-e X ] && ...` lead-ins (matching EXISTENCE_ONLY_RE's own alternation); a content search chained after a `stat`/`ls` existence probe, or chained with `;` instead of `&&`, is not covered by this round's fix and would need a follow-up if that shape turns out to matter in practice

SILENT_SEARCH_RE recognises `grep -q`/`grep --quiet` specifically (including combined short flags like `-iq`); a different silent-by-design search tool (e.g. a custom script that also prints nothing) chained the same way is not covered by this round's sibling-existence-check requirement at all, so it still falls into the 'no captured output, not silent-search-shaped' rejection branch above it — this was scoped to the exact tool Greptile's finding used, not every possible silent search command

ABSENCE_CLAIM_RE now requires a path/file/directory noun next to the ambiguous words (exists/absent/removed/deleted/gone), or one of a fixed set of unambiguous phrases (no longer exists/no longer present/not present/does not exist); a differently-worded content-vs-path distinction outside both of those shapes — e.g. an absence claim that names neither a path noun nor one of the listed phrases — would still fall through to the existence-only rejection, and a content-removal claim that happens to mention the word 'file' in passing (e.g. 'the token was removed from the file's header comment') could still wrongly pass; this was scoped to the exact ambiguity Greptile's finding demonstrated, not an exhaustive claim-intent parser

This round's fix (Greptile's remaining technical P1, tip_match 2/5): a quiet-grep compound (`test -f X && grep -q PATTERN X` / `[ -f X ] && grep -q PATTERN X`) now requires a SEPARATE command in the same receipt that is a bare existence check (EXISTENCE_ONLY_RE) naming the same path and exiting 0, or it is rejected as exhaustive evidence — closing the gap where a missing file and a real quiet no-match produced the identical exit code and empty output. The sibling-existence-check exception to the pre-existing 'no other commands' padding rule is scoped narrowly (only a bare existence check on the exact same path counts; any other extra command, including one that also proves existence via a non-EXISTENCE_ONLY_RE shape like `find . -name X`, is still treated as padding and rejected) — this is intentionally conservative/fail-closed, consistent with the rest of this gate's heuristics, not an exhaustive parser of every way existence could be proven

The sibling-existence-check match (`_is_positive_existence_check`) tests `path in other_cmd` as a plain substring, not a shell-aware tokenizer — a sibling command whose argument differs only by quoting or an unrelated prefix/suffix overlap (e.g. testing `config/.env.example.bak` would substring-match a gate_path of `.env.example`) could in principle satisfy the corroboration requirement when it does not actually prove the same file existed; this mirrors the substring-based path matching already used elsewhere in this gate (e.g. MISSING_TARGET_RE's quoted-text stripping) rather than introducing a new class of approximation, but it was not specifically probed with an adversarial near-match path in this round's tests

This gate does not verify that the sibling existence-check command actually ran BEFORE the quiet-grep compound it corroborates — 'commands' is not asserted to be in chronological execution order anywhere else in this file either, so a receipt could record the corroborating `test -f X` after the compound command and still pass; this is a pre-existing property of the receipt schema (no command timestamps are required), not a new gap introduced by this fix, but it means the sibling check proves 'X existed at some recorded point', not strictly 'X existed when the compound ran'
